sections.title: Habit and habitat
sections.text: Cirriphyllum piliferum is a pleurocarpous moss forming branched mats, with shoots sometimes more than 10 cm long. Its feathery branches bear concave leaves 2–2.5 mm long, each ending in a fine hair point. It grows on sheltered, often shaded soils, banks, rocks and old walls.

sections.title: Features and plate
sections.text: Sporophytes and capsules are uncommon; the plate focuses on the mat and leaves, which is consistent. A moss has no flowers or fruits, and no food use is known.
